questions.question: When traveling slower than 40 mph, keep at least ____ of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Below 40 mph, allow one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At faster speeds, use the same formula and add one more second. Large vehicles need more space to stop than small vehicles.

questions.question: If you use the trailer hand brake while your trailer is skidding, it will:
questions.explanation: Using the trailer hand brake during a skid will make the skid worse. To stop a trailer jackknife, release the brakes so your tires can grip the road again.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should be used:

options.text: Regularly to activate the trailer brakes in all driving conditions.
Only to test the trailer brakes.
Only in inclement weather when the trailer may skid.
Only if the trailer is carrying a load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: Use the trailer hand valve only to test the trailer brakes. Do not use it while driving because it can cause the trailer to skid.

questions.question: To prevent a trailer from rolling over, you should:

options.text: Speed up when nearing a corner.
Take on-ramps faster than the posted speed limit.

questions.explanation: To prevent rollovers, keep cargo as low to the ground as possible and drive slowly around turns.

questions.question: Operating combination vehicles usually requires ____ operating single vehicles.

options.text: About the same level of skill as

questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are heavier and longer than single commercial vehicles. They require more driving skill to operate safely.

questions.question: Combination vehicles:

options.text: Are usually shorter than single commercial vehicles.
Are usually lighter than single commercial vehicles.
Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
Are easier to drive than single commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Require more skill to drive than single commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are heavier and longer than single commercial vehicles. They require more driving skill.

questions.question: To help prevent rollovers, you should:

options.text: Keep the load near the back of the trailer.
Keep the load on one side of the trailer.

questions.explanation: To prevent rollovers, place cargo as low to the ground as possible and take curves and corners slowly.

questions.question: To control surge when stopping, you should not:

options.text: Keep a steady pressure on the brakes.
Brake well in advance of a stop.

questions.explanation: To prevent surge in a tank vehicle, brake early with steady pressure and do not release the brakes too quickly. Keep a larger following distance.

questions.question: A tractor protection valve is:

options.text: A device that keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system, should the trailer break away or develop a bad leak.
A device that controls fuel levels.
A device that allows the battery to recharge efficiently.

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system, should the trailer break away or develop a bad leak.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a bad leak.

questions.question: The best way to recognize that your trailer has begun to skid is by:
questions.explanation: The best way to spot a trailer skid early is to see the trailer slide off-course in your mirrors.

questions.question: If a load is placed on one side of a trailer, what could happen?

options.text: The trailer may lean and could roll over.
The trailer will have extra support during turns.
The trailer will have better braking.
The trailer will have better steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer may lean and could roll over.
questions.explanation: When weight is on one side of a trailer, the trailer may lean. This increases the risk of a rollover.

questions.question: What does a tractor protection valve do?

options.text: Keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
Prevents a truck from being stolen.
Prevents a trailer from being accidentally released.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the brake system if the trailer breaks away or if there is a bad leak. The valve closes automatically when the pressure gets too low.

questions.question: What can the "crack-the-whip" effect do?
questions.explanation: Trailers can tip over because of the "crack-the-whip" effect. The last trailer in a combination is most likely to tip. Drivers should know about this rearward movement and drive carefully.

questions.question: When should a trolley valve be used?

options.text: Only to test the trailer brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trolley valve controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Do not use it while driving because it could cause a skid. Do not use it while parking because it may release the air pressure and the brakes holding the vehicle.

questions.question: How should you test the tractor protection valve?

options.text: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To test the tractor protection valve: Let the air supply charge fully, turn off the engine, then press the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to its emergency position when the pressure gets too low.

questions.question: What happens when you push in the trailer air supply control?

options.text: Air is supplied to the trailer.
The air brakes are turned off.
The vehicle is prevented from skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air is supplied to the trailer.
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull it out to stop the air supply and engage the emergency brakes.

questions.question: When braking with ABS, how should you press the brake pedal?

options.text: The same as you normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as you normally would.
questions.explanation: With an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), apply the brakes the same way you would without ABS.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: When you plan an escape route.

questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers take turns too fast.

questions.question: ____ cause more than half of all accident-related truck driver deaths.
questions.explanation: More than half of accident-related truck driver deaths are caused by truck rollovers. To prevent rollovers: load cargo low and centered on your truck, and take corners slowly and carefully.

questions.question: During a trip, which valves should be open?
questions.explanation: When you start a trip, open all shut-off valves except the last ones on the rear trailer. This allows air to reach the brakes on all trailers and prevents air from escaping from the back of the vehicle.
